_meta.description: Drone configuration presets from COEP Hexacopter v4 Multi-Path Analysis

presets.name: Path G-A (Recommended)
presets.description: 6× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 1× 30Ah Semi-Solid + 10L tank. Only viable option within E616P frame limit.
presets.notes: 16 min flight. 2.5x thrust margin. Import-only battery (30-day lead time).
pros: Fits the ₹4.0L target budget
Hexacopter architecture
Open-source ArduPilot FC (best for research)
36 kg MTOW (2.5:1 thrust margin with X8)
16 min flight time (covers 1 mission + reserve)
1× 30Ah Semi-Solid battery (1,332 Wh, 4.9 kg)
GPS has compass (HGLRC M100-5883)
8 build-quality items included
Fits your RC plane experience
cons: Tattu 30Ah 12S needs import
Combinations_notes: Uses 1× Tattu 30Ah Semi-Solid battery (imported, 20-30 day lead time) to keep MTOW within the E616P 36 kg frame limit.
Hobbywing X8 motors (instead of X9 G2L) are chosen because they are lighter and cheaper, yet still provide a safe 2.5:1 thrust margin (6.0 kg/axis) at the corrected 36 kg MTOW.
Non-RTK GPS (HGLRC M100-5883 w/ compass) is used to save ₹23,000 while preserving position-hold, RTL, and auto modes in ArduPilot.
Pixhawk 6C is chosen over Cube Orange+ to save ₹17,500.
No radar or Mauch sensor to keep the build cost within the ₹4.0L target.

presets.name: Path G-B (2× 22Ah In-Stock)
presets.description: 6× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 2× Tattu 22Ah Pro + 10L tank. Uses in-stock batteries but exceeds frame limit.
presets.notes: In-stock batteries. 23 min flight. MTOW ~43kg exceeds E616P 36kg limit.
pros: Uses 2× Tattu 22Ah Pro which are in stock locally
Hexacopter architecture
Open-source ArduPilot FC
cons: 2× 22Ah adds 6.7 kg, pushing MTOW to ~43 kg
Exceeds E616P 36 kg frame limit
Combinations_notes: Uses 2× Tattu 22Ah Pro (in-stock in India) to avoid the 30-day battery import lead time of the 30Ah pack.
Using 2× 22Ah Pro batteries adds 6.7 kg to the build, pushing the MTOW to ~43 kg, which exceeds the EFT E616P frame's rated 36 kg limit.
Although it's a budget-friendly option (saves on import), it is structurally unviable for the E616P frame due to excessive weight.

presets.name: Path A (Jiyi Closed-Source)
presets.description: 6× X8 + Jiyi K++V2 + 2× Tattu 22Ah + 10L tank. Teacher's RFQ literal. Closed-source FC.
presets.notes: Closed-source FC. Built-in spray logic. Out of stock at Zbotic.
pros: All teacher RFQ line items (where available) used
Cheapest commercial-spray path
Best fit for closed-source Jiyi ecosystem (spray logic built-in)
cons: Below recommended 5-7 kg/axis thrust for X8
10L tank vs v7's 16L spec — payload reduced
Closed-source FC limits research documentation
Combinations_notes: Follows the teacher's literal RFQ using a Jiyi K++ V2 closed-source FC kit and Skydroid H12 Pro remote controller.
Uses 2× Tattu 22Ah Pro batteries.
Cheapest commercial-spray path with built-in agricultural spray logic, but closed-source FC limits research documentation.
Below recommended 5-7 kg/axis thrust for X8 motors at the corrected MTOW (which exceeds the E616P's 36 kg limit).

presets.name: Path B (X9 G2L + RFD868x)
presets.description: 5× X9 G2L + Pixhawk 6C + 1× 30Ah + 16L tank. Premium motors with DroneCAN telemetry.
presets.notes: X9 G2L = DroneCAN per-motor telemetry. SHURflo imported. 18 min flight.
pros: Open-source FC (ArduPilot) — best for research
X9 G2L gives 4× thrust margin at 30 kg MTOW
1× 30Ah battery (not 2× 22Ah) — saves ₹25k vs v7 spec
DroneCAN ESC telemetry per-motor
cons: Tattu 30Ah 12S is hard to source in India at retail
SHURflo pump is imported ($110 USD) — lead time 2-3 weeks
Combinations_notes: Uses 1× Tattu 30Ah Semi-Solid battery to save ₹25k vs 2× 22Ah.
Uses Hobbywing X9 G2L motors which provide a high thrust margin (4x) at 30 kg MTOW.
DroneCAN protocol is used for per-motor ESC telemetry.
Uses imported SHURflo diaphragm pump ($110 USD) which has a 2-3 week lead time.

presets.name: Path C (8× X8 Hybrid)
presets.description: 8× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 2× Tattu 22Ah + 16L tank. Most spares, RC-plane-friendly PWM.
presets.notes: 8 motors = most expensive. 4 spare props. 18 min flight. Exceeds frame.
pros: All Hobbywing X8 (PWM ESC) — fits your RC plane background
Open-source ArduPilot FC
Most spares (4 spare props)
Within X8 recommended 5-7 kg/axis range
cons: Most expensive of the 6 paths
No per-motor telemetry (X8 reports only RPM, not current)
Combinations_notes: Fits the user's RC plane background by using Hobbywing X8 motors with PWM ESC signals (50-500Hz).
Uses 2× Tattu 22Ah Pro smart batteries, which exceeds the E616P's 36 kg frame limit at the corrected weight.
Pixhawk 6C open-source flight controller is selected for research capability.
Most expensive of the 6 legacy paths because it includes 4 spare propellers (2 of each direction).

presets.name: Path D (Quad-X Budget)
presets.description: 4× X9 G2L + Pixhawk 6C + 1× 30Ah + 10L tank. Cheapest but loses hexa redundancy.
presets.notes: Quad = no motor-out redundancy. Cheapest path. 22 min flight.
pros: Cheapest path (₹3.01L)
25 kg MTOW (best thrust margin in X9 G2L range)
26.5 min flight time
Less complex assembly (4 motors)
cons: Loses 1-motor-out redundancy (hexa has it; quad does not)
Ma'am specified hexacopter
Combinations_notes: Simplifies the architecture to a 4-motor Quadcopter (Quad-X) using a generic 1200mm T700 frame, saving ₹18,000 on the frame.
Uses Hobbywing X9 G2L motors (4 motors instead of 6) to achieve a high thrust margin and 26.5 minutes of flight time.
Saves cost and reduces complexity, making it the cheapest path at ₹3.01L, but loses 1-motor-out redundancy and deviates from Ma'am's hexacopter specification.

presets.name: Path F (₹3.5L Aggressive)
presets.description: 6× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 1× 22Ah + 10L tank. Hard budget cap, minimal spares.
presets.notes: 1× 22Ah only = 12 min flight. No spare props. Single GPS.
pros: Fits the ₹3.5L aspirational budget
Hexacopter architecture (preserves ma'am spec)
Open-source FC
cons: 23 min flight time — barely enough for 1 mission
1× GPS (no redundancy) — single point of failure
No spare props
No RTK (not a research-feature now)
22 kg MTOW (10L tank at full)
Combinations_notes: Designed to meet a strict ₹3.5L budget limit.
Achieves savings by utilizing a single 22Ah Pro battery, which reduces flight time to ~12 minutes (barely 1 mission).
Removes spare props, RTK GPS, and redundant sensors to cut costs.
Uses Matek BEC instead of MAUCH current sensor to save ₹5k.
Meant for demonstration purposes only, not recommended for real production due to lack of safety margins and short flight time.

presets.name: PH-1    combined Hexa
presets.description: 6× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 2× GenX 22Ah (Indian) + Tarot T960 + Custom 7L HDPE tank. Maximum cost savings with open-source everything. Great for lab flight testing and hackathon demos.
presets.notes: ~14 min hover flight (2× 22Ah). 5L spray at full throttle. T960 MTOW ~25kg sufficient for 7L payload. ELRS 2.4GHz rx pairs with RadioMaster TX16S.    combined tank must be custom-fabricated with pump inlet at bottom.
pros: Lowest cost among all hexacopter builds — ₹2.93L all-in
All components India-stocked — zero import wait time
GenX batteries available from Robu.in with next-day delivery
ELRS open standard — longer range than FrSky at lower cost
TFmini-S LiDAR adds altitude-hold for impressive hackathon demos
Tarot T960 is foldable — easy transport to field/venue
Full ArduCopter + QGroundControl support — free, open-source GCS
Custom HDPE tank saves ₹2,800+ and can be any shape/size needed
cons: T960 frame not rated for 10L+ payload — limited to 7L custom tank
HGLRC M100 GPS is single-constellation — no GLONASS backup
Custom tank requires local fabrication effort — not plug-and-play
Tarot T960 arm clamps must be verified for X8 motor tube diameter
No spare props included — any crash grounds the drone immediately
GenX batteries not as battle-tested as Tattu for high-current agri use
5L pump + 7L tank means short spray window (~4 min at 1.5 L/min)
Combinations_notes: Tarot T960 replaces EFT frame — saves ₹26,499. Foldable, community-supported, rated to ~25kg MTOW with X8 motors.
GenX 22Ah 12S LiPo (Indian brand, Robu-stocked) replaces Tattu — saves ₹21,674 per pack.
Custom 7L HDPE tank (fabricated locally at any plastics shop) replaces branded EFT tank — saves ₹2,825.
BetaFPV ELRS Lite 2.4GHz RX replaces FrSky — saves ₹325, ELRS has longer range.
HGLRC M100 GPS replaces Holybro M9N — saves ₹6,901, adequate for non-RTK work.
Benewake TFmini-S LiDAR adds terrain-following/altitude-hold capability for hackathon demo points.

presets.name: PH-2 Research Hexa
presets.description: 6× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 2× GenX 22Ah + EFT E610P + 10L tank + TFmini-S LiDAR. Solid research-grade platform on a controlled budget. Suitable for COEP lab use, paper experiments, and hackathon showcases.
presets.notes: ~15 min hover (2× GenX 22Ah). 5L spray @ 1.5 L/min. EFT E610P fits 6× X8 comfortably. Dual-constellation GPS for research data quality. TFmini-S altitude logging adds research value. ArduCopter fully supported.
pros: EFT E610P is a purpose-built agricultural frame — proper motor mounts, cable management, IP-rated
Holybro M9N GPS: GPS + GLONASS + BeiDou — multi-constellation for research accuracy
2× GenX batteries give ~15 min hover — adequate for field experiments
Matek FCHUB-12S PDB has built-in 5V/12V BEC — cleaner wiring than Tarot PDB
TFmini-S LiDAR enables altitude data logging — publishable in research papers
All components India-stocked — no import dependency
Saves ₹43,000 over Tattu battery option while getting more total energy
COEP lab-deployable — EFT frame has peer community documentation in India
cons: EFT E610P supports up to 10L — cannot scale to 16L tank without frame upgrade
5L pump may be underpowered for future experiments requiring higher flow rates
TFmini-S is short-range (12m) — not suitable for high-altitude terrain following
No RTK GPS — positioning accuracy is ~1-3m, not cm-level
No dual-GPS redundancy — single point of failure for navigation
GenX batteries: lower brand recognition in academic publications vs Tattu
Matek PDB less current headroom (100A continuous) vs Tarot TL2996 (480A)
Combinations_notes: GenX 22Ah replaces Tattu 22Ah Pro — Indian-sourced, saves ₹21,674/pack, in-stock at Robu.
EFT E610P frame chosen over E616P — rated for 10L payload, saves ₹6,999, lighter by 1.2kg.
Matek FCHUB-12S PDB replaces Tarot TL2996 — cleaner cable routing, integrated BEC, saves ₹1,732 but adds signal filtering.
Holybro M9N GPS (multi-constellation) upgrades from HGLRC — proper research-grade GNSS, GPS+GLONASS+BeiDou.
Holybro 10A dual BEC provides clean 5V+12V rails for FC and peripherals.
Benewake TFmini-S adds radar altimeter functionality — publishable altitude data for research papers.

presets.name: PH-3 TiHAN Demo
presets.description: 6× X8 + Cube Orange+ + 1× Tattu 30Ah Semi-Solid + EFT E616P + 16L tank + Here4 RTK + TF03 LiDAR + backup M9N GPS. Maximum capability build for TiHAN/IITH demonstration — RTK precision, dual-IMU FC, full sensor suite.
presets.notes: ~16 min flight with 16L (est.). RTK GPS enables cm-accuracy positioning logs. Cube Orange+ dual-IMU = research-publishable IMU data. TF03 LiDAR is industrial grade — terrain-following at 100m range. Demo-ready for TiHAN/IITH audience. Tattu 30Ah is import (30-day lead time).
pros: Here4 RTK GPS: cm-level accuracy positioning — required for precision agri research papers
Cube Orange+ dual-IMU with temperature control — highest IMU data quality available at this price
ADS-B carrier on Cube Orange+ — compliant with airspace regulations out of the box
Dual-GPS setup (Here4 RTK primary + M9N backup) — hot-failover, highest safety margin
TF03 100m LiDAR: IP65 rated, industrial grade — terrain following at 100m range
16L tank with 8L pump — full agricultural spray mission capacity
EFT E616P frame — purpose-built for 16L agri use, proven in field
Demo-ready appearance — looks professional for TiHAN/IITH audience presentation
cons: Most expensive preset at ₹4.57L — highest budget required
Tattu 30Ah is import-only — 30-45 day lead time from China, plan early
Single battery = no hot-swap redundancy on field
Here4 RTK requires a base station (additional ₹15,000-40,000) for true RTK accuracy
Cube Orange+ has steeper setup curve than Pixhawk 6C for beginners
TF03 LiDAR is overkill for most lab flights — adds cost without benefit unless terrain-following is required
Higher MTOW than PH-1/PH-2 due to heavier 16L tank system
Combinations_notes: Cube Orange+ chosen over Pixhawk 6X — dual IMU (with temperature control), ADS-B carrier, broader ArduCopter support, research community standard.
Here4 RTK GPS enables cm-level positioning — publishable for precision agriculture research, required for TiHAN-level credibility.
Holybro M9N added as backup GPS — dual-GPS hot-failover for safety.
Hobbywing 8L pump (over 5L) for 16L tank — matches flow rate to tank capacity, avoids 2× spray time.
Benewake TF03 100m LiDAR — proper industrial altitude sensor, 100m range, IP65 rated, academic citation-worthy.
Only non-   combined in the list: Tattu 30Ah Semi-Solid. No cheaper Indian alternative at this spec/weight exists.

presets.name: PH-4 Budget Spray Proto
presets.description: 6× X8 + Pixhawk 6C + 1× GenX 22Ah + Tarot T960 + Custom 7L HDPE tank. Minimum viable spray demonstration drone for initial lab testing and proof-of-concept flights. Not for endurance — for validating spray system.
presets.notes: ~8 min hover (1× 22Ah). Short flight is intentional — this is a test rig not a field drone. T960 rated ~25kg with X8 motors. 7L HDPE custom tank is the key    combined. GenX battery is India-stocked. Start here, upgrade to PH-1 or PH-2 after validation.
pros: Cheapest complete hexacopter spray build possible — ₹2.63L
All India-sourced components — buy and start building same week
Perfect for first-time builders — learn on this before spending more
If crashed/damaged, total loss is manageable — intentional risk budget
Validates entire spray system (pump, nozzles, tank, flow) at low cost
Same motors, FC, and ESC as higher presets — component knowledge transfers up
Can upgrade to PH-1 by just adding 1 battery + LiDAR — modular path
cons: ~8 min flight time — barely enough for spray system validation, not field use
No LiDAR — relies solely on barometric altitude, no terrain following
Single battery with no swap means ground time between flights is ~45 min (charge cycle)
T960 frame is not IP-rated — not suitable for wet/dusty field conditions
Custom HDPE tank is DIY — requires fabrication skill and time
No spare props — a single prop strike grounds the build
Not demo-worthy for TiHAN/IITH audience — purely a prototype rig
HGLRC GPS provides no GLONASS — weak satellite lock in obstructed areas
Combinations_notes: 1× battery only (not 2×) — reduces flight time to ~8 min but slashes cost. Enough for spray system validation.
Tarot T960 frame used — cheap, widely available, community-documented for X8 motor mounting.
Custom 7L HDPE tank (fabricated at local plastic fabricator, <₹3,000) — enough for 3-4 minutes of spray at 1.5 L/min.
Minimal consumables — no spare props initially, no LiDAR, no redundant sensors.
ELRS receiver vs FrSky — longer range for the same price, works with free OpenTX/EdgeTX on Radiomaster.
Matek 12V BEC (not Holybro dual BEC) — saves ₹1,000. Sufficient for single rail applications.
This preset is explicitly: build-fly-break-learn. Not for demos. For system validation.

presets.name: PH-5 Cube Research
presets.description: 6× X8 + Cube Orange+ + 2× GenX 22Ah + EFT E616P + Here4 RTK + TF03 LiDAR + 16L tank + RPi NoIR camera. Full open-source research platform — Cube FC, RTK GPS, LiDAR altimeter, vision logging. The best build for publication-level research without going full commercial.
presets.notes: ~14-15 min hover (2× GenX 22Ah). 16L spray capacity. Full open-source — no proprietary lockouts. Here4 RTK enables cm-accuracy logs for agri precision data. RPi NoIR + 850nm IR filter = basic NDVI sensor. Cube Orange+ dual-IMU is the research-grade standard at CubePilot ecosystem labs. Best balance of cost and capability for MTech/paper-level work.
pros: Cube Orange+ is the CubePilot research ecosystem standard — used by IITH, IITB, IISc labs
Here4 RTK: cm-level GPS accuracy — publishable precision agri positioning data
2× GenX 22Ah gives more total energy than 1× Tattu 30Ah at ₹58,000 less cost
RPi NoIR camera enables basic NDVI crop health imaging — adds research dimension
TF03 100m LiDAR enables real terrain-following for canopy spraying experiments
Fully open-source stack — ArduCopter, MAVLink, QGC, Mission Planner, no vendor lock-in
16L tank + 8L pump = full agricultural spray profile for meaningful field experiments
EFT E616P frame is field-proven for 16L agri payload — not a prototype frame
Best overall value for MTech thesis or hackathon requiring publication-quality data
cons: Here4 RTK needs a ground-based RTK base station for true cm accuracy — extra ₹15k-40k
Cube Orange+ requires more setup time than Pixhawk 6C — steeper learning curve
RPi NoIR camera needs additional software (ROS/OpenCV) for NDVI processing
No backup GPS — single Here4 RTK is single point of navigation failure
2× GenX batteries wired in parallel need proper anti-spark parallel connector (XT90-S)
EFT E616P approaches MTOW limit with 16L liquid + all components — marginal thrust margin
Higher total cost (₹3.99L) than PH-1/PH-2 — requires larger initial funding
Combinations_notes: Cube Orange+ over Pixhawk 6X — comparable capability, stronger community support (COEP/IITH labs use CubePilot ecosystem).
GenX 22Ah replaces Tattu — 2× GenX = ₹48,000 vs 1× Tattu 30Ah at ₹1,06,000. Almost equal energy at half the cost.
Here4 RTK GPS — mandatory for research-publishable cm-accuracy positioning. Worth every rupee for a thesis or paper.
RPi NoIR camera — adds video logging, IR plant health assessment, and NDVI capability when paired with 850nm filter.
EFT 16L tank gives full spray mission profile — meaningful experiment duration.
TF03 100m LiDAR — terrain-following for variable-height canopy spraying, critical for real agri research.
Hobbywing 8L pump matches 16L tank — do not use 5L pump with 16L tank, spray time doubles unnecessarily.
No DJI components — fully open-source stack. ArduCopter + MAVLink + QGroundControl + Mission Planner.
